description: Re1 is a one-person team: a photographer from Basel, Switzerland, who builds small, private web tools for images.
summary: A small online museum of the human machines and objects left on the Moon and Mars. Each exhibit is one card: a photo, a short true story, and one line that stays with you — from the Apollo 15 "Fallen Astronaut" and Charlie Duke's family photo to Opportunity, Spirit, InSight and Ingenuity. It turns a list of abandoned hardware into memory: why it was left, what it did, how it ended. It works on any phone, needs no installation, and is bilingual (English/Spanish). Every fact is checked against NASA sources, and popular myths are clearly marked.
details:
What it does: The museum shows 15 exhibits — 7 on the Moon, 8 on Mars. Visitors can filter by world, open any exhibit to read its story, and switch between English and Spanish with one tap.

How it works: A single HTML page with no frameworks, no tracking and no login. Images use small thumbnails so it loads fast even on slow mobile connections. Hosted for free on GitHub Pages.

Why it matters: Most people know the famous landings, but not what was left behind. These objects are part of our shared heritage. Telling their stories in a simple, human way helps the public — especially non-scientists — care about them.

Honesty: Every fact is real and checkable against NASA sources. Popular myths are clearly marked, e.g. Opportunity's "my battery is low and it's getting dark" is a journalist's line, not a real transmission.

About the creator: I am an independent photographer based in Basel, Switzerland. My craft is telling stories with images; this project applies that to space history.
